main_text.l: Μηδ' ἐπιορκήσεις, μητ' ἀγνῶς, μηδὲ ἐκῶν πῃ
Nam miser est quisquis temere periuria fundit,
Cum veniat tacitis poena frequens pedibus.

page.notes: The woodcut shows a figure with a sword in the right hand, scales in the left, standing on a globe, with the sun above and a coastal town with scales at the right. The Greek line is printed as shown; its final words are hard to read and may be wrong. The verse lines end with a printed dash or stop; the italic long s is transcribed as s.
